title: Chapter 3: How Dorothy Saved the Scarecrow

paragraphs.en: When Dorothy was left alone she began to feel hungry. So she went to the cupboard and cut herself some bread, which she spread with butter. She gave some to Toto, and taking a bucket from the shelf she carried it down to the little brook and filled it with clear, sparkling water. Dorothy was a innocent, good-hearted little girl, and she resolved to prepare for her long journey to the Emerald City.
paragraphs.zh: 当多萝茜独自留下来时她开始感到饥饿。于是她走到碗橱前给自己切了一些面包，抹上了黄油。她给了一些给托托，并从架子上拿了一个水桶提到小溪边装满了清澈闪烁的水。多萝茜是一个纯真、善良的小女孩，她决定为她前往翡翠城的漫长旅程做准备。

paragraphs.en: She walked along the Yellow Brick Road until she stopped to rest beside a cornfield. Perched on a pole in the middle of the field was a Scarecrow, stuffed with straw, dressed in a blue suit, and painted with a comical face. To Dorothy's utter surprise, the Scarecrow winked at her and spoke: 'Good day!'
paragraphs.zh: 她沿着黄砖路行走，直到停在一个玉米田旁休息。栖息在田野中央杆子上的是一只稻草人，里面塞满了稻草，穿着一套蓝色衣服，画着一张滑稽的脸。令多萝茜完全吃惊的是，稻草人向她眨了眨眼并说话了：“美好的一天！”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy helped him climb down from the pole. The Scarecrow explained that he was miserable because he had no brain inside his painted head. 'I don't mind my legs and arms being stuffed with straw,' he said, 'but I hate to be called a fool because I have no brains.' Dorothy invited him to join her journey to ask Oz for a brain, and the Scarecrow happily accepted.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝茜帮助他从杆子上爬了下来。稻草人解释说他很悲惨，因为在他的画头上里面没有脑子。“我不介意我的腿和手臂塞满稻草，”他说，“但我讨厌因为没有脑子而被叫做傻瓜。”多萝茜邀请他加入她的旅程去向奥兹要脑子，稻草人快乐地接受了。

paragraphs.en: The Yellow Brick Road wound onward through the magical countryside of Oz, flanked by sparkling brooks, colorful wild flowers, and strange golden trees. Dorothy tightly held Toto in her arms, her magical Silver Shoes sparkling with every step she took toward their goal.
paragraphs.zh: 黄砖路沿着奥兹国奇幻的乡村继续盘旋，两侧环绕着闪烁的小溪、绚丽的野花与神奇的金树。多萝茜把托托紧抱在怀里，她魔法银鞋在她朝目标迈出的每一步中都闪闪发光。

paragraphs.en: 'No matter how dreary our home in Kansas may be,' Dorothy remarked softly to the Scarecrow, 'we people of flesh and blood would rather live there than in any other country, be it ever so beautiful. There is no place like home.'
paragraphs.zh: '无论我们在堪萨斯的家多么沉闷，'多萝茜对稻草人软软地注意到，'我们血肉之躯的人们宁愿住在那里，也不愿住在任何其他国家（无论它多么美丽）。没有任何地方像家一样。'
